sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our Salzburg data is recent, so there is no city trend yet; the figures below are for weekdays and weekends in August and September 2026, partly in the tourist season.

Salzburg's parking politics turn on one question: whether to add capacity under the Mönchsberg. In January 2022 the Parkgaragengesellschaft's supervisory board voted to expand the Mönchsberg garage by 654 spaces for €39.8 million, with critics noting it had been full on only 49 days in 2021 [5]. In a city survey in June 2022 about 84% of valid votes rejected the expansion, on a turnout of 22% [6]. The city is now planning the other way. A Mobilitätsplan 2040 aims to cut the share of motorised private transport from about 37% to 20% by 2040, with measures from 2027 [12], and a parking concept to 2036 is being planned in three stages: more short-term zones and €1.30 per half hour to 2028, a special Altstadt tariff zone around 2029–2032, and number-plate payment checked by camera cars. These are plans, which local businesses and two parties have criticised [11].

Under the council's parking-fee ordinance the fee has been €1.10 per half hour since January 2026 [0]. In summer 2026 the city restricted car access to the central routes along the Salzach from 1 July, mainly to residents, regional commuters and hotel guests. Three weeks in, the city said traffic had flowed more smoothly than feared and park-and-ride ticket sales were up more than 50% on the previous year at Salzburg Süd, with a final evaluation planned for year-end [13]. A state referendum on extending the S-LINK rail to Hallein, rejected by 53%, was ruled unlawful by the Constitutional Court in December 2025 [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
We found no sources on new garages opening in the centre. The city's efforts have gone into getting drivers to park outside. In 2023 the city and Salzburg AG agreed a uniform €15 day price at the Salzburg Süd and Messezentrum park-and-ride sites, including public transport tickets for up to five people, with a €5 all-day ticket planned for July and August at the Messezentrum [10]. A Green councillor said uptake of these sites had stagnated at a low level for years [10]. The Altstadtgaragen under the Mönchsberg hold 1,298 spaces, with 20 spaces for electric cars [3][4]. The garage company is 60% owned by the city and 40% by the state, and after the 2022 vote the mayor floated using about €6 million of accumulated funds for other purposes, including renovating the fairground garage for park-and-ride, as proposals [7].

On technology, the city was running a pilot in 2022 to give navigation-app providers live occupancy data for 13 larger garages and car parks, so that summer visitors can be steered to park-and-ride, with digital road signs still to come [8]. Visitor demand is high: the province reported a record 30.5 million overnight stays in the year to October 2025 [16], and annual network tickets in the province grew from about 50,000 in 2018 to nearly 120,000 in early 2026 [15].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
Salzburg's central garages are expensive. The Altstadtgarage charges €3.60 an hour, up from €3.30 at the start of 2026, with a €25.90 day maximum, Mirabell €4.50 and €40 a day, and the station garage €2.40; the park-and-ride at Salzburg Süd costs €1 an hour [1]. The ordinance's €1.10 per half hour equals €2.20 an hour, below the central garages' rates [0]. Our tariff data lists Contipark for most of the central garages, Best in Parking for the Linzergasse garage and APCOA for the Auersperg garage; we have not confirmed these from the garages' own pages.

Use is moderate and fairly even across the centre. The 12 garages we measure average 39% on weekdays and 35% at weekends. The station garage is the fullest (74%), followed by the small Auersperg garage (58%), Akademiestraße (60% on weekdays but only 7% at weekends) and the Linzergasse garage (52%). Mirabell, at the highest price, stands at 51%. Altstadtgarage A runs at 44% and B at 30%. The garages farther out are quieter: the Salzburg Süd park-and-ride at 30% and the Tiergarten Hellbrunn car park at 9%.
